interpretation: The first 50 actions are similar, but the trajectories diverge later, consistent with stochastic policy sampling and closed-loop scene differences.
Both runs make coherent progress and fail at the fixed horizon, so failure is not explained by a dead actuator, invalid action mapping, or inference outage.
The second run is much faster in wall-clock inference but still fails at step 700; network latency affects test duration, not the simulated control-step budget.

root_cause_assessment.primary: The policy uses mostly sequential pick-and-place behavior. Its observed per-object cycle time leaves insufficient horizon to deposit four bottles and satisfy the terminal return-home condition within 700 controls (28 simulated seconds).
secondary: Late-run stochastic divergence changes whether two or three bottles are completed by the cutoff.
The action chunk is open-loop for 50 controls between observations, limiting correction opportunities during each grasp/transfer cycle.
not_supported_by_evidence: Mechanical control failure: joint tracking errors remain small.
NPU compute failure: all 14 inferences completed with stable ~0.56 s device time.
Network delay as the task failure cause: wall-clock latency changed greatly between repeats while both had the same 700-step failure.
remaining_uncertainty: Automatic reward integration is still invalid because reward_manager.step() is not called.
Camera/action/state alignment matches the configured adapter, but official success-rate equivalence still requires the official evaluator path and multiple seeds.
